content: Before starting aprepitant and each time you receive a refill, carefully read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, refer to the Instructions for Use sheet for detailed guidance on its proper administration. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your physician. The first dose is typically taken one hour prior to the initiation of chemotherapy. For the subsequent two days, continue taking one dose daily, one hour before the start of treatment, if chemotherapy is scheduled for that day. The dosage of aprepitant is determined based on your medical condition, age, and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also calculated according to their weight. It is crucial to adhere to your doctor’s instructions regarding the timing, duration, and strength (in milligrams) of each dose. Common side effects may include fatigue or hiccups. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has assessed that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking aprepitant, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to fosaprepitant, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of aprepitant from your body, potentially altering its efficacy. Examples include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), diltiazem, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), nefazodone, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., nelfinavir), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Aprepitant can either accelerate or slow the elimination of other medications from your body, which may impact their effectiveness. If you are taking warfarin, this drug may influence how well warfarin works in your system. Additionally, aprepitant may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication and for one month after the last dose. Aprepitant is closely related to fosaprepitant. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. Store the capsules at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. The liquid form should be refrigerated and any unused liquid should be discarded after 72 hours. Do not freeze the liquid. When ready to use, the liquid form may be kept at room temperature for up to three hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
